\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Complex-Valued Functions on Finite Tuples]
\lean{FABL.AbelianL2}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p227-b004}
\label{FABL.AbelianL2}
\leanok
For a type $G$ and a natural number $n$, let $\ell^2(G^n;\mathbb{C})$ denote the space
of complex-valued functions on $n$-tuples of elements of $G$, namely the functions
$(\mathrm{Fin}(n)\to G)\to\mathbb{C}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Uniform complex inner product]
\lean{FABL.complexUniformInner}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p240-b005,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p240-b008
}
\statementsource{ghsz-combinatorial-list-decoding}{pdf-6bd33ae73ade-p005-b002}
\label{FABL.complexUniformInner}
\leanok
For a finite set $\Omega$ and functions $f,g:\Omega\to\mathbb{C}$, define their uniform
complex inner product by averaging $\overline{f(x)}g(x)$ over $x\in\Omega$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Uniform complex mean]
\lean{FABL.complexMean}
\label{FABL.complexMean}
\leanok
For a finite set $\Omega$ and a function $f:\Omega\to\mathbb{C}$, its complex mean is
the uniform average $\frac{1}{|\Omega|}\sum_{x\in\Omega}f(x)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Complex covariance]
\lean{FABL.complexCovariance}
\label{FABL.complexCovariance}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.complexMean, FABL.complexUniformInner}
For a finite set $\Omega$ and complex-valued functions $f,g$ on $\Omega$, their complex
covariance is the complex uniform inner product of the centered functions $x\mapsto
f(x)-\mathbb{E}_{\Omega}f$ and $x\mapsto g(x)-\mathbb{E}_{\Omega}g$, where
$\mathbb{E}_{\Omega}$ denotes uniform averaging on $\Omega$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Complex variance]
\lean{FABL.complexVariance}
\label{FABL.complexVariance}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.complexCovariance}
For a finite set $\Omega$ and a complex-valued function $f$ on $\Omega$, its complex
variance is the complex covariance of $f$ with itself.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Self inner product as a mean square]
\lean{FABL.complexUniformInner_self_eq_expect_absSq}
\label{FABL.complexUniformInner_self_eq_expect_absSq}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.complexUniformInner, FABL.complexUniformInner_eq_expect}
\difficulty{1}
Let $	ext{Omega}$ be a finite set and let $f:	ext{Omega}	oC$. The uniform inner
product of $f$ with itself equals the uniform mean of $|	ext{f}(x)|^2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Probability weighted complex inner product]
\lean{FABL.pmfComplexInner}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p240-b005,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p240-b008
}
\label{FABL.pmfComplexInner}
\leanok
For a finite set $\Omega$, a probability mass function $p$ on $\Omega$, and functions
$f,g:\Omega\to\mathbb{C}$, define their probability weighted complex inner product as
$\sum_{x\in\Omega}p(x)\,\overline{f(x)}g(x)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Probability-weighted complex mean]
\lean{FABL.pmfComplexMean}
\label{FABL.pmfComplexMean}
\leanok
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set, let $p$ be a probability mass function on $\Omega$, and
let $f:\Omega\to\mathbb{C}$. The $p$-weighted complex mean of $f$ is
$\sum_{x\in\Omega}p(x)f(x)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Orthonormal Fourier system]
\lean{FABL.ComplexFourierSystem}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p023-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p024-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p091-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p227-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p227-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p240-b005,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p240-b008
}
\statementsource{ghsz-combinatorial-list-decoding}{pdf-6bd33ae73ade-p005-b002}
\label{FABL.ComplexFourierSystem}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.pmfComplexInner}
Let $\Omega$ and $\iota$ be finite sets. A complex Fourier system on these sets consists
of a probability mass function $\mu$ on $\Omega$ that assigns positive mass to every
point, a basis $(\phi_i)_{i\in\iota}$ of the complex vector space of functions on
$\Omega$, and a distinguished index $i_0\in\iota$. The distinguished basis function is
constant one, and the basis is orthonormal for the inner product weighted by $\mu$:
$\sum_{x\in\Omega}\mu(x)\overline{\phi_i(x)}\phi_j(x)=1$ when $i=j$ and $0$ otherwise.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Fourier coefficient]
\lean{FABL.ComplexFourierSystem.coeff}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p022-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p091-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p211-b002
}
\statementsource{ghsz-combinatorial-list-decoding}{pdf-6bd33ae73ade-p005-b002}
\label{FABL.ComplexFourierSystem.coeff}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ComplexFourierSystem}
Given a complex Fourier system on finite sets $\Omega$ and $\iota$, a function
$f:\Omega\to\mathbb{C}$, and an index $i\in\iota$, define the $i$th Fourier coefficient
of $f$ to be its coordinate at $i$ in the basis of the system.
\end{definition}

Let $F$ be a complex Fourier system on finite sets $Ω$ and $ι$, with a full-support
probability law and an orthonormal basis containing the constant-one function at a
distinguished index. For every complex-valued function $f$ on $Ω$ and every $x\in Ω$,
$f(x)=\sum_{i\in ι}\widehat f(i)\,b_i(x)$, where $\widehat f(i)$ is the coefficient of
$f$ at $i$ and $b_i$ is the $i$th basis function.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Inner product of a finite linear combination]
\lean{FABL.ComplexFourierSystem.pmfComplexInner_sum_right}
\label{FABL.ComplexFourierSystem.pmfComplexInner_sum_right}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.pmfComplexInner}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\Omega$ and $I$ be finite sets, let $p$ be a probability mass function on $\Omega$,
and let $f:\Omega\to\mathbb C$, $a:I\to\mathbb C$, and $g:I\to(\Omega\to\mathbb C)$.
Then $\left\langle f,\sum_{i\in I}a(i)g_i\right\rangle_p=\sum_{i\in I}a(i)\langle
f,g_i\rangle_p$, where the sum of functions is taken pointwise and
$\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_p$ is the probability-weighted complex inner product.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Conjugate symmetry of the probability inner product]
\lean{FABL.ComplexFourierSystem.pmfComplexInner_conj_symm}
\label{FABL.ComplexFourierSystem.pmfComplexInner_conj_symm}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.pmfComplexInner}
\difficulty{3}
Let $Ω$ be a finite set, let $p$ be a probability mass function on $Ω$, and let
$f,g:Ω\to\mathbb C$. The complex conjugate of their probability-weighted inner product
is the same inner product with $f$ and $g$ interchanged.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Linearity in the second argument]
\lean{FABL.ComplexFourierSystem.pmfComplexInner_smul_right}
\label{FABL.ComplexFourierSystem.pmfComplexInner_smul_right}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.pmfComplexInner}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set, let $p$ be a probability mass function on $\Omega$, and
let $f,g:\Omega\to\mathbb C$ and $c\in\mathbb C$. The probability-weighted complex inner
product satisfies $\langle f,cg\rangle_p=c\langle f,g\rangle_p$, where $\langle
f,g\rangle_p=\sum_{x\in\Omega}p(x)\overline{f(x)}g(x)$.
\end{theorem}

probability law and an orthonormal basis containing the constant-one function at a
distinguished index. For every complex-valued function $f$ on $Ω$ and every $i\in ι$,
the probability-weighted inner product of $f$ with the $i$th basis function is the
complex conjugate of the coefficient of $f$ at $i$.
\end{theorem}

probability law and an orthonormal basis containing the constant-one function at a
distinguished index. For any complex-valued functions $f,g$ on $Ω$, their
probability-weighted inner product equals $\sum_{i\in ι}\overline{\widehat
f(i)}\,\widehat g(i)$, where the coefficients are taken in the chosen basis.
\end{theorem}

Let $F$ be a complex Fourier system on finite sets $Ω$ and $ι$, with a full-support
probability law and an orthonormal basis containing the constant-one function at a
distinguished index. For every complex-valued function $f$ on $Ω$, its
probability-weighted squared norm equals the sum of the squared absolute values of its
Fourier coefficients: $\langle f,f\rangle=\sum_{i\in ι}\overline{\widehat
f(i)}\,\widehat f(i)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Mean under a Fourier system]
\lean{FABL.ComplexFourierSystem.mean}
\label{FABL.ComplexFourierSystem.mean}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ComplexFourierSystem, FABL.pmfComplexMean}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set equipped with a probability law $p$, and let
$f:\Omega\to\mathbb{C}$. The mean associated with a complex Fourier system having law
$p$ is $\sum_{x\in\Omega}p(x)f(x)$.
\end{definition}

probability law and an orthonormal basis containing the constant-one function at a
distinguished index $i_0$. For every complex-valued function $f$ on $Ω$, its mean under
the law of $F$ equals its Fourier coefficient at $i_0$.

\begin{theorem}[Linearity of Fourier coefficients]
\lean{FABL.ComplexFourierSystem.coeff_sub}
\label{FABL.ComplexFourierSystem.coeff_sub}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ComplexFourierSystem, FABL.ComplexFourierSystem.coeff}
\difficulty{1}
Let $F$ be a complex Fourier system on finite sets $␀Ω$ and $␀ι$, with a full-support
probability law and an orthonormal basis containing the constant-one function at a
distinguished index. For any complex-valued functions $f,g$ on $␀Ω$ and any index
$i␀∈ι$, the coefficient of $f-g$ at $i$ is the coefficient of $f$ at $i$ minus the
coefficient of $g$ at $i$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Fourier coefficients of a constant]
\lean{FABL.ComplexFourierSystem.coeff_const}
\label{FABL.ComplexFourierSystem.coeff_const}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ComplexFourierSystem, FABL.ComplexFourierSystem.coeff, FABL.ComplexFourierSystem.coeff_eq_inner, FABL.ComplexFourierSystem.pmfComplexInner_smul_right}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\Omega$ and $\iota$ be finite sets, and let $F$ be a Fourier system on $\Omega$
with a full-support probability law, an orthonormal basis of complex-valued functions,
and a distinguished index for the constant-one basis vector. For any complex constant
$c$ and any basis index $i$, the coefficient of the constant function with value $c$ is
$c$ at the distinguished index and zero at every other index.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Fourier coefficients after centering]
\lean{FABL.ComplexFourierSystem.coeff_centered}
\label{FABL.ComplexFourierSystem.coeff_centered}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ComplexFourierSystem, FABL.ComplexFourierSystem.coeff, FABL.ComplexFourierSystem.coeff_const, FABL.ComplexFourierSystem.coeff_sub, FABL.ComplexFourierSystem.mean, FABL.ComplexFourierSystem.mean_eq_coeff_zero}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\Omega$ and $\iota$ be finite sets, and let $F$ be a Fourier system on $\Omega$
with a full-support probability law, an orthonormal basis of complex-valued functions,
and a distinguished index for the constant-one basis vector. For any complex-valued
function $f$ and any basis index $i$, the coefficient of $f$ minus its mean is zero at
the distinguished index and equals the coefficient of $f$ at every other index.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Complex covariance]
\lean{FABL.ComplexFourierSystem.covariance}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p014-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p027-b005
}
\label{FABL.ComplexFourierSystem.covariance}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ComplexFourierSystem, FABL.ComplexFourierSystem.mean, FABL.pmfComplexInner}
Given a complex Fourier system on finite sets $\Omega$ and $\iota$, and functions
$f,g:\Omega\to\mathbb{C}$, define their covariance as
$\sum_{x\in\Omega}\mu(x)\overline{(f(x)-\mathbb{E}_{\mu}f)}(g(x)-\mathbb{E}_{\mu}g)$,
where $\mu$ is the system's probability law and $\mathbb{E}_{\mu}$ denotes expectation
under that law.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Complex variance]
\lean{FABL.ComplexFourierSystem.variance}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p018-b006,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p027-b001
}
\label{FABL.ComplexFourierSystem.variance}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ComplexFourierSystem, FABL.ComplexFourierSystem.covariance}
Given a complex Fourier system on finite sets $\Omega$ and $\iota$, and a function
$f:\Omega\to\mathbb{C}$, define its variance as the covariance of $f$ with itself.
\end{definition}

Let $F$ be a complex Fourier system on finite sets $Ω$ and $ι$, with a full-support
probability law and an orthonormal basis containing the constant-one function at a
distinguished index $i_0$. For any complex-valued functions $f,g$ on $Ω$, their
covariance under the law of $F$ equals $\sum_{i\in ι,\ i\ne i_0}\overline{\widehat
f(i)}\,\widehat g(i)$, where $\widehat f(i)$ and $\widehat g(i)$ are their coefficients
in the chosen basis.
\end{theorem}

  {FABL.zmodProductCharacterAddEquiv}
  {context}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p228-b010,
    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p228-b011}
\proofstep
  {FABL.zmodProductFourierBasis}
  {direct}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p228-b010}
\proofstep
  {FABL.zmodProductFourierBasis_apply}
  {context}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p228-b010}
Let $\Omega$ and $I$ be finite sets, and let $p$ be a probability mass function on
$\Omega$ that assigns positive mass to every point. Suppose $(\phi_i)_{i\in I}$ is an
orthonormal basis of the complex-valued functions on $\Omega$ for the inner product
$\langle f,g\rangle_p=\sum_{x\in\Omega}p(x)\overline{f(x)}g(x)$, and that $\phi_{i_0}$
is the constant-one function for a distinguished index $i_0\in I$. For any
$f:\Omega\to\mathbb C$, its variance, defined as $\langle f-\mathbb E_p f,f-\mathbb E_p
f\rangle_p$ with $\mathbb E_p f=\sum_xp(x)f(x)$, equals $\sum_{i\in I,\ i\ne
i_0}|\widehat f(i)|^2$, where $\widehat f(i)$ is the coefficient of $\phi_i$ in the
basis expansion of $f$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Character of an abelian group]
\lean{FABL.AbelianCharacter}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p023-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p091-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p227-b006
}
\statementsource{ghsz-combinatorial-list-decoding}{pdf-6bd33ae73ade-p005-b002}
\label{FABL.AbelianCharacter}
\leanok
For an additive abelian group $G$, an abelian character is an additive group
homomorphism from $G$ to the additive group of complex numbers.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Dual of an abelian group]
\lean{FABL.AbelianDual}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p091-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p228-b011,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p229-b002
}
\label{FABL.AbelianDual}
\leanok
For an additive abelian group $G$, its abelian dual is the collection of additive group
homomorphisms from $G$ to the additive group of complex numbers.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Conjugate of a character]
\lean{FABL.characterConj}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p228-b002}
\label{FABL.characterConj}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.AbelianCharacter}
For an additive commutative group $G$ and a complex-valued additive character $\chi$ on
$G$, define its conjugate character to be the pointwise inverse character $\chi^{-1}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Conjugation of a character]
\lean{FABL.characterConj_apply}
\label{FABL.characterConj_apply}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.AbelianCharacter, FABL.characterConj}
\difficulty{3}
Let $G$ be a finite additive commutative group, let $\chi:G\to\mathbb C$ be an additive
character, and let $x\in G$. The conjugate character evaluated at $x$ is the complex
conjugate of $\chi(x)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Product with a conjugate character]
\lean{FABL.characterMulConj}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p228-b002}
\label{FABL.characterMulConj}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.AbelianCharacter, FABL.characterConj}
For an additive commutative group $G$ and complex-valued additive characters $\phi$ and
$\chi$ on $G$, define their product with conjugation by $\phi\chi^{-1}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Product with a conjugate character]
\lean{FABL.characterMulConj_apply}
\label{FABL.characterMulConj_apply}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.AbelianCharacter, FABL.characterConj_apply, FABL.characterMulConj}
\difficulty{3}
Let $G$ be an additive commutative group, let $\phi,\chi:G\to\mathbb C$ be additive
characters, and let $x\in G$. Their product character, formed from $\phi$ and the
conjugate character associated with $\chi$, takes the value $\phi(x)\overline{\chi(x)}$
at $x$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Fourier coefficient of a function]
\lean{FABL.abelianFourierCoeff}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p022-b001,

\leanok
\uses{FABL.AbelianCharacter, FABL.complexUniformInner}
For a finite additive commutative group $G$, a function $f:G\to\mathbb{C}$, and a
complex-valued additive character $\chi$ on $G$, define the Fourier coefficient of $f$
at $\chi$ to be the uniform complex inner product of $\chi$ with $f$.
\end{definition}

Let $G$ be a finite abelian group and let $f,g:G\to\mathbb{C}$. Their uniform inner
product equals the sum over all additive characters $\chi$ of $G$ of the complex
conjugate of the Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $\chi$, multiplied by the Fourier
coefficient of $g$ at $\chi$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Fourier coefficient of a difference]
\lean{FABL.abelianFourierCoeff_sub}
\label{FABL.abelianFourierCoeff_sub}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.AbelianCharacter, FABL.abelianFourierCoeff, FABL.complexUniformInner_eq_expect}
\difficulty{3}
Let $G$ be a finite abelian group, let $f,g:G\to\mathbb{C}$, and let $\chi$ be an
additive character of $G$. The Fourier coefficient of $f-g$ at $\chi$ is the Fourier
coefficient of $f$ at $\chi$ minus that of $g$ at $\chi$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Fourier coefficients of constants]
\lean{FABL.abelianFourierCoeff_const}
\label{FABL.abelianFourierCoeff_const}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.AbelianCharacter, FABL.abelianFourierCoeff, FABL.characters_orthonormal, FABL.complexUniformInner, FABL.complexUniformInner_eq_expect}
\difficulty{4}
Let $G$ be a finite abelian group, let $c\in\mathbb{C}$, and let $\chi$ be an additive
character of $G$. The Fourier coefficient of the constant function with value $c$ is $c$
at the trivial character and zero at every other character.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Centered Fourier coefficients]
\lean{FABL.abelianFourierCoeff_centered}
\label{FABL.abelianFourierCoeff_centered}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.AbelianCharacter, FABL.abelianFourierCoeff, FABL.abelianFourierCoeff_const, FABL.abelianFourierCoeff_sub, FABL.complexMean, FABL.complexMean_eq_abelianFourierCoeff_zero}
\difficulty{4}
Let $G$ be a finite abelian group, let $f:G\to\mathbb{C}$, and let $\chi:G\to\mathbb{C}$
be an additive character. The Fourier coefficient of $f$ after subtracting its uniform
mean is zero when $\chi$ is the trivial character, and otherwise equals the Fourier
coefficient of $f$ at $\chi$.
\end{theorem}

of $f$ with itself equals the sum, over all additive characters $\chi$ of $G$, of the
squared absolute values of the Fourier coefficients of $f$ at $\chi$.
\end{theorem}

  {FABL.zmodProductFourierBasis_apply}
  {context}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p228-b010}
Let $G$ be a finite abelian group and let $f:G\to\mathbb{C}$. The variance of $f$ under
the uniform distribution on $G$ equals the sum, over all nontrivial characters $\chi$ of
$G$, of the squared absolute values of its Fourier coefficients:
$\operatorname{Var}(f)=\sum_{\chi\ne 1}\overline{\widehat f(\chi)}\,\widehat f(\chi)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Character of a cyclic residue group]
\lean{FABL.zmodCharacter}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p228-b008}
\label{FABL.zmodCharacter}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.AbelianCharacter}
For a positive natural number $m$ and $j\in\mathbb{Z}/m\mathbb{Z}$, define the
associated complex-valued additive character on $\mathbb{Z}/m\mathbb{Z}$ by the standard
additive-group character corresponding to $j$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Zmod character injective]
\lean{FABL.zmodCharacter_injective}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p228-b008}
\label{FABL.zmodCharacter_injective}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.zmodCharacter}
\difficulty{1}
% dataset-pipeline: stub -- prose pending build_informal_statements.py
Statement pending regeneration.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Integer Formula for a Cyclic Character]
\lean{FABL.zmodCharacter_intCast}
\label{FABL.zmodCharacter_intCast}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.zmodCharacter}
\difficulty{3}
For every positive integer $m$ and all integers $j,x$, the cyclic character indexed by
the residue of $j$ modulo $m$, evaluated at the residue of $x$, equals $\exp\!\left(2\pi
i\,\frac{jx}{m}\right)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Fourier basis on a cyclic residue group]
\lean{FABL.zmodFourierBasis}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p228-b008,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p228-b009
}
\label{FABL.zmodFourierBasis}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.abelianFourierBasis}
For a positive natural number $m$, the complex-valued functions on
$\mathbb{Z}/m\mathbb{Z}$ have a basis over $\mathbb{C}$ indexed by
$\mathbb{Z}/m\mathbb{Z}$, obtained by indexing the character basis of this finite
additive group by residue classes.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Cyclic Fourier Basis Vectors]
\lean{FABL.zmodFourierBasis_apply}
\label{FABL.zmodFourierBasis_apply}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.zmodCharacter, FABL.zmodFourierBasis}
\difficulty{1}
For every positive integer $m$ and every residue $j$ modulo $m$, the Fourier basis
vector indexed by $j$ is the cyclic character indexed by $j$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Product character on a finite power]
\lean{FABL.zmodProductCharacter}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p228-b010}
\label{FABL.zmodProductCharacter}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.AbelianCharacter, FABL.zmodCharacter}
For positive $m$, a natural number $n$, and a tuple $\alpha=(\alpha_i)_{i=1}^n$ of
elements of $\mathbb{Z}/m\mathbb{Z}$, define a complex-valued additive character on
$(\mathbb{Z}/m\mathbb{Z})^n$ by sending $x=(x_i)_{i=1}^n$ to $\prod_{i=1}^n
\chi_{\alpha_i}(x_i)$, where $\chi_{\alpha_i}$ is the character associated to
$\alpha_i$.
\end{definition}

For every positive integer $m$, every natural number $n$, and functions
$\alpha,x:\{0,\ldots,n-1\}\to\mathbb Z/m\mathbb Z$, the product character indexed by
$\alpha$, evaluated at $x$, equals $\prod_{i=0}^{n-1}\chi_{\alpha(i)}(x(i))$, where
$\chi_j$ denotes the cyclic character indexed by $j$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Product character at zero]
\lean{FABL.zmodProductCharacter_zero}
\label{FABL.zmodProductCharacter_zero}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.AbelianCharacter, FABL.zmodCharacter, FABL.zmodProductCharacter}
\difficulty{4}
Let $m>0$ and let $n$ be a natural number. The product character indexed by the zero
function on $\mathrm{Fin}(n)$ is the trivial character on $(\mathbb Z/m\mathbb Z)^n$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Homomorphism from indices to product characters]
\lean{FABL.zmodProductCharacterHom}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p227-b006,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p228-b010
}
\label{FABL.zmodProductCharacterHom}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.AbelianCharacter, FABL.zmodCharacter, FABL.zmodProductCharacter, FABL.zmodProductCharacter_zero}
For positive $m$ and a natural number $n$, the map sending each tuple
$\alpha\in(\mathbb{Z}/m\mathbb{Z})^n$ to the product character
$x\mapsto\prod_{i=1}^n\chi_{\alpha_i}(x_i)$ is an additive-group homomorphism into the
group of complex-valued additive characters on $(\mathbb{Z}/m\mathbb{Z})^n$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Product Character on a Single Coordinate]
\lean{FABL.zmodProductCharacter_apply_single}
\label{FABL.zmodProductCharacter_apply_single}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.zmodCharacter, FABL.zmodProductCharacter, FABL.zmodProductCharacter_apply}
\difficulty{5}
For every positive integer $m$, every natural number $n$, every function
$\alpha:\{0,\ldots,n-1\}\to\mathbb Z/m\mathbb Z$, every index $i\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$,
and every residue $y$ modulo $m$, the product character indexed by $\alpha$, evaluated
on the vector equal to $y$ at coordinate $i$ and zero elsewhere, equals
$\chi_{\alpha(i)}(y)$, where $\chi_j$ denotes the cyclic character indexed by $j$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Product-group character equivalence]
\lean{FABL.zmodProductCharacterAddEquiv}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p229-b002}
\label{FABL.zmodProductCharacterAddEquiv}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.AbelianDual, FABL.zmodProductCharacterHom, FABL.zmodProductCharacter_injective}
For every positive integer $m$ and natural number $n$, the additive group $(Z/mZ)^n$
is additively equivalent to its group of complex-valued additive characters.
\end{definition}

$\alpha,\beta:\{0,\ldots,n-1\}\to\mathbb Z/m\mathbb Z$, the product character indexed by
the pointwise sum $\alpha+\beta$ is the pointwise product of the product characters
indexed by $\alpha$ and $\beta$.
\end{theorem}

$\alpha\colon\{0,\ldots,n-1\}\to\mathbb Z/m\mathbb Z$. The product character indexed by
$-\alpha$ is the pointwise inverse of the product character indexed by $\alpha$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Fourier basis for a product group]
\lean{FABL.zmodProductFourierBasis}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p228-b010}
\label{FABL.zmodProductFourierBasis}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.abelianFourierBasis, FABL.zmodProductCharacterAddEquiv}
For every positive integer $m$ and natural number $n$, the complex-valued functions on
$(Z/mZ)^n$ have a basis indexed by the elements of $(Z/mZ)^n$, obtained by indexing
the abelian Fourier basis using the product-group character equivalence.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Product Fourier basis vectors]
\lean{FABL.zmodProductFourierBasis_apply}
\label{FABL.zmodProductFourierBasis_apply}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.abelianFourierBasis_apply, FABL.zmodProductCharacter, FABL.zmodProductFourierBasis}
\difficulty{3}
Let $m>0$ and let $n$ be a natural number. For every function
$\alpha\colon\mathrm{Fin}(n)\to\mathbb Z/m\mathbb Z$, the Fourier basis vector indexed
by $\alpha$ is the product character indexed by $\alpha$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Circle characters and multiplicative group]
\lean{FABL.circleCharacterMulEquiv}
\label{FABL.circleCharacterMulEquiv}
\leanok
For a finite abelian group $G$, the group of additive characters from $G$ to the circle
group is isomorphic as a multiplicative group to the multiplicative version of $G$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Circle characters and additive group]
\lean{FABL.circleCharacterAddEquiv}
\label{FABL.circleCharacterAddEquiv}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.circleCharacterMulEquiv}
For a finite abelian group $G$, the group of additive characters from $G$ to the circle
group is isomorphic as an additive group to $G$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Finite abelian dual equivalence]
\lean{FABL.abelianDualAddEquiv}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p228-b011,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p229-b002
}
\label{FABL.abelianDualAddEquiv}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.AbelianDual, FABL.circleCharacterAddEquiv}
For every finite abelian group $G$, its group of complex-valued additive characters is
additively equivalent to $G$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Finite abelian double duality]
\lean{FABL.abelianDoubleDualAddEquiv}
\label{FABL.abelianDoubleDualAddEquiv}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.AbelianDual}
For a finite additive commutative group $G$, the canonical additive equivalence
identifies $G$ with the group of additive characters of its character group.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Normalized convolution on a finite abelian group]
\lean{FABL.abelianConvolution}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p030-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p229-b003
}
\label{FABL.abelianConvolution}
\leanok
For a finite abelian group $G$ and functions $f,g:G	obc$, define their normalized
convolution at $xr G$ to be $|G|^{-1}rsum_{y+z=x} f(y)g(z)$.
\end{definition}

  {FABL.abelianConvolution}
  {context}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p229-b003}
Let $G$ be a finite abelian group, and let $f,g:G\to\mathbb C$. Their normalized
convolutions satisfy $f*g=g*f$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Associativity of normalized convolution]
\lean{FABL.abelianConvolution_assoc}
\label{FABL.abelianConvolution_assoc}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.abelianConvolution, FABL.abelianConvolution_apply}
\difficulty{4}
Let $G$ be a finite abelian group, and let $f,g,h:G\to\mathbb C$. Their normalized
convolution is associative: $(f*g)*h=f*(g*h)$.
\end{theorem}

  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p229-b003}
Let $G$ be a finite abelian group, and let $f,g:G\to\mathbb{C}$ and $\chi$ be an
additive character of $G$. The Fourier coefficient at $\chi$ of the normalized
convolution of $f$ and $g$ is the product of their Fourier coefficients at $\chi$.
\end{theorem}
